description: Heuristic vs DP instruction selector on random IR trees: MATCH-TREE DP (supplementary Appendix D.1) vs the shipped greedy heuristic tree cover. Sizes 20/50/100/200 nodes x 5 seeds; metrics are covering cost and wall-clock selection time.

provenance.rng_seed_formula: random.Random(size * 1000 + seed) per (size, seed); catalogue and tree use independent streams from the same seed

notes: Costs are catalogue instruction costs summed over the covering (MATCH-TREE total cost); lower is better.

The invariant under test is DP cost <= heuristic cost (structural: the DP minimises over a covering set that includes the greedy single-node covering); the ABSOLUTE gap depends on this synthetic catalogue's pricing model.

Catalogue pricing: fused patterns cost 0.70-0.95x the base cost of (root op + spanned child ops) while covering the spanned children's whole subtrees, so one fused site near the root can subsume a large subtree -- the cost gap grows with tree size by construction of the model, not by magic.
Premium variants (1.3-2.0x base cost, carrying the urgency param) are only ever chosen by the score-first heuristic; the cost-minimising DP never selects them.
Timing is wall-clock selection time (median of reps); DP being slower is allowed and reported honestly.
The heuristic arm is the shipped greedy tree cover (single-node patterns only, no cross-node horizon); the DP arm is MATCH-TREE (Appendix D.1).
Aggregates are computed by this script from the raw per-instance records via the statistics module; nothing is hand-filled.
